correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=2 and positive hazard vector, monotone cumulative-hazard transformation gives independent exponentials. Conditional-on-winner memorylessness makes the minimum Exp(sum rates) independent of the residual maximum. Finite inclusion-exclusion proves the signed exponential residual-density formula. Difference of independent minima is a symmetric Laplace law, giving tau=E exp(-Lambda|G-Gcopy|). Split-domain integration of two exponential terms gives the exact rational pair kernel; finite summation yields the theorem. For n=2 the formula simplifies algebraically to (1-t)(3-t)/(9-t); its first derivative is -(t^2-18t+33)/(9-t)^2 <0 and second derivative 96/(9-t)^3>0, proving the inverse and optimal derivative constants at both parameter boundaries. Exact-rational verifier passed 144 two-rate, 5 homogeneous, 51 heterogeneous, and 3 fixed-reference checks; simulations corroborate but are not proofs.

originality.rationale: The directly covering 2008 predecessor explicitly stops at an upper bound on Kendall concordance and calls exact heterogeneous calculation complex despite deriving the full copula. The 2022 PHR improvement proves a dependence ordering, not an unequal-rate finite concordance sum. The 2005 and 2018 explicit rank formulas require common parent marginals. No published-finding corpus or web search found the new evaluated finite formula together with two-rate baseline-free inversion. The underlying copula is prior work and is explicitly acknowledged; priority risk from older equivalent algebraic evaluations remains.
residual_risks: The 2010 Navarro–Balakrishnan full text could not be inspected, though its published abstract restricts explicit concordance to exchangeable or iid parents.
Equivalent rank-concordance calculations may appear in older reliability papers or differently parameterized copula literature.

value.rationale: Dependence of earliest and latest component failures is a natural series-parallel reliability statistic. Earlier PHR work supplied comparative order and a bound; the evaluated exact formula gives rate-resolved concordance for every finite heterogeneous system and any common baseline. In the minimal nontrivial two-component case, rank concordance identifies an unordered hazard ratio with explicit sharp sensitivity constants, a structural identification theorem relevant to baseline-free calibration. These are complete natural invariant statements rather than a small arbitrary numerical exercise. No claim of efficient large-n computation or statistical inference is made.
